about: What's new, shown once when the app opens (whats-new.js). Hand-edited: add one short plain line at the TOP of items for each change people will notice, with today's date. Newest first.

items.text: Tap or drag anywhere on the map (2D or 3D) and it stops following you. Tap Recenter (or Follow while riding) to follow again.
Skiing cabin trips: the card now says Not finished when some offline files are still missing, and Saved only when it all is.
Offline maps: Pick a square shows a square right away with big corners to drag, and a big green Saved or orange Not saved box says if it worked. Missing files are tried again by themselves.
Skiing cabin trips: the way in now starts where the road is plowed, and unplowed logging roads count as part of the ski in.
How it works is much shorter: one or two lines per feature, opening on your sport's part.

Skiing: huts show as brown house pins when you zoom in, with a green “Book” tag when they must be booked. Tap one to see the price, beds, heat and water, and a Book button that opens the club's booking page.
Skiing: plan a cabin trip. Tap a hut, then 🏕 Plan a cabin trip here: pick your dates, see the easiest way in from the parking, the avalanche danger and weather for each day, and save it all offline.
Skiing: tap a hut and its card pops up right away, and hut names show beside the dots when you zoom in close.
Skiing 3D no longer runs out of memory with Snow and rain forecast or the radar on: the 3D map now frees the old pictures each time those layers update.
3D map in every sport: a soft photo shows right away after you move or zoom out, instead of blank ground or holes to the sky while the sharp photos load.
Skiing 3D: the ground fills in faster after you move, with a soft winter photo instead of grey patches while the sharp one loads.
The map Key button now moves up above the radar, clouds and smoke bars on phones, so it no longer sits on top of their colour key.
Faster on phones: typing a trail name in search no longer freezes the keyboard, and zooming out over new trails stays smoother.
Skiing: Snow forecast and New snow also show rain (in greens) where it rains instead, make the 3D map lag less, and no longer leave dark patches when the weather service is busy.
Skiing: the Whistler snow stake cam now plays the live video (it was a picture that refreshed each minute).
Skiing: the Whistler snow stake cam now shows the live picture of the new snow stake (it showed an old summer picture before).
3D map: pins for far-away places (webcams, huts, lifts, ski areas, parking) no longer float in the sky above the mountains. Pins on slopes you can see stay put.

Skiing 3D: Snow forecast and New snow now colour the whole view, far distance included. Before, wide views asked the weather service for too much at once and some squares stayed bare (dark patches) for an hour.

Layers that colour the whole ground (Avalanche risk, Slope angle, New snow, Snow forecast, Forest types, Mud and more) now show one at a time: turning one on turns the other off, so the map stays readable and lighter on your phone.

Skiing: tap anywhere and the This spot card now shows the snow that fell in the last 24 h, 3 days and 7 days, the snow forecast for the next 24 h, 3 days and 7 days, and the weather day by day for the past week and the week ahead. New snow and Snow forecast now turn each other off, so only one shows at a time.
Skiing: the Whistler snow stake cam is on the map with the other Whistler Blackcomb webcams, so you can see how much new snow fell.
Hunting: drop pins and tag them: trail cam, tracks, saline, cache, stand, rub, scrape, bait, kill site, parking, other and more. A pin can have several tags, and Saved filters your pins by tag.
Hunting: the map no longer freezes when you zoom out over a whole province, and zone names no longer pile on top of each other.

Hunting: new Property lines layer shows the lines between lots (Quebec cadastre, BC, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia; Ontario lots and concessions, Alberta sections). Zoom in close and tap a spot for the lot number.
Fishing: creeks and streams now show from a whole-valley zoom, Crown land works in BC (private land in yellow), and tapping a BC lake gives its scanned depth map.

Yukon: hunting seasons for every game management subzone (tap the map in Hunting), and fishing limits for each Yukon lake and river with its own rules, like Fish Lake, Lake Laberge and the Yukon River at Whitehorse.
Photo find asks where a picture was taken when only the AI guessed the place, then compares it with riders' pictures of every trail there.
Skiing 3D: the mountains come up about twice as fast when you open it, and the 3D map uses less of your phone's memory so it runs out less.

Live lift status at Revelstoke, Lake Louise, RED Mountain and Mont-Sainte-Anne, lake depths in Alberta (169 lakes) and Nova Scotia (634 lake maps), and backcountry ski cards for Fish Lake near Whitehorse and the Tablelands in Gros Morne.
The app opens faster: Skiing, Hunting, Fishing and Moto now load only when you pick them.
Real trail ratings for Fernie, the Cranbrook Community Forest and Penticton's Three Blind Mice, from the local trail clubs' and regional district's own maps.
Search finds towns and trails anywhere in Canada: type Bromont and the map goes there.
Trail heights now load even when the weather service is busy, and shuttle routes warn you about gates to check (🚧).
New trails now shows the list right away, the app finds you even if you skip the welcome, and Prime loam tells you which day the dirt turns prime when nothing is prime today.
3D winter photos now cover Cumberland, Prince George, Whitehorse and Hardwood too.
Ski heatmap: much more around Whistler, the Spearhead and the Callaghan. Slackcountry past the resort gates is no longer cut out, and tours recorded with fewer GPS points now count.
Fishing and Hunting in New Brunswick, Nova Scotia and Newfoundland and Labrador: fishing areas with their rules, and hunting seasons for each zone.
Skiing webcams: the Brandywine Bowl sled cam near Whistler, four Coquihalla sled cams (parking lot to the 10-K cabin), and alpine station cams at Plummer Hut, Klinaklini and the Cruickshank valley.
Sharper satellite map in Ontario and around Lake Louise, Sunshine and Banff: the province's and the park's own air photos.
Logging areas now work everywhere in Canada: outside BC, Alberta and Quebec they show forest cut or burned since 2010, seen from space.
Skiing: live lift status at Tremblant, Blue Mountain and Bromont.
Skiing webcams: live highway cameras near Smithers, Whitehorse, Sugarloaf, Wentworth, Blue Mountain and Marble, and Mont-Sainte-Anne's 6 cameras in the app.
Fishing: Layers has picture tiles to highlight all rivers, all lakes, creeks, the ocean, lake depths and Crown land, on the flat and 3D map.
Find: tap 📍 under the search box to change area; no match looks in all areas.
Loops: after opening a loop on the map, tap ← Loops to go back to the same list and pick another.
iPhone app: loam, avalanche and stocking alerts now arrive as real iPhone notifications.
iPhone app: while you record, your time, km, climb and the trail you're on show on the lock screen and in the Dynamic Island.
iPhone app: a popup tells you when a newer version is ready in TestFlight.
Fishing: lake depth lines now cover Ontario, Quebec and Manitoba too (plus New Brunswick soundings), and a lake's card links its depth map where the province has one.
Sharper Summer photos in Quebec and New Brunswick: the provinces' own air photos (15-20 cm) where the satellite photo was blurry, in 2D and 3D.
Better outside Whistler: all of Quebec's fishing zones, Smithers, Nanaimo, Medicine Hat and other riding areas show their bike trails, and webcam links for 7 eastern ski hills.
New: Ask in plain words, in every sport. Type "2-hour loop in prime loam near Squamish tomorrow" on the Find page and the app answers from its own trails, loam, tours and maps.

Crown land across Canada: public land in green and private land in yellow from each province's own map (Ontario, Quebec, the Maritimes, Saskatchewan, Newfoundland, Manitoba forests). In Hunting, Moto and Fishing, and tap a spot to see who owns the land.
Share your live location: friends and family follow you on a map from a link, with a "back by" time (Ride or Track page, and More).
New 🌧 Radar layer: see rain or snow falling now and the last 3 hours, all over southern Canada.
Adventure moto: plan a route and get a new one when you go off it, even with no signal, from the roads in your saved offline maps.
Skiing 3D: the ground is always whole now. Cloudy spots in last winter's photo are filled with a snowy photo before they show, and the map lags less.
MTB now opens on the flat map the first time. After that, each sport opens on the map you last left it on (3D or flat, map style and layers).
Skiing 3D: no more blue holes and broken-looking mountains where last winter's photo was cloudy (Grouse, Seymour, Kicking Horse and others). Those spots now show the snowy photo instead.

Skiing: the avalanche colours now change slope by slope. Steep slopes facing today's avalanche problems turn a level hotter (red can show at treeline too), gentle or sheltered slopes a level cooler. Tap a slope to see why.
The 3D map no longer slowly fills the phone's memory as you move around, so long Skiing sessions shouldn't restart the app any more.
On the phone, swipe the map's bottom card down to shrink it to just the search bar and see more map. Swipe it up (or tap the handle) to bring it back.

Every sport now looks the same on the phone: a search box and a Today line on the map, and each sport's tab in the same order (search, Today, 4 big buttons, a list, what's on the map). The map key is one Key button, bottom left.
Offline maps now work in every sport: Hunting saves its zones and layers, Fishing its waters and rules, and you can save the 3D map too (in Skiing with last winter's photos).
First-time visitors now get a short welcome: pick a sport, allow location, the basics.
New Help and support and Privacy pages in More, and you can now delete your account in Account → Settings.
Skiing: the Winter 3D map gets sharper up close on phones too (trees, rocks and snow bumps show as you zoom in).
Skiing: tapping a spot keeps the map where it is (it no longer zooms out on the 3D map).
Skiing: tap a route to see its conditions at a glance: weather at the top and bottom, avalanche danger on the route, visibility (in or above the clouds) and the snow, for today or the next two days.

Skiing: tap any empty spot on the map (flat or 3D) to see its slope angle, which way it faces, height, terrain class, avalanche danger for that band, new and coming snow, wind loading and the closest route, hut and snow station.
Skiing: tapping a 📷 webcam pin opens the live camera again, on the flat and 3D map, even where it sits on a lift.
Skiing 3D on phones: the Winter photos fill in about twice as fast after you move, and close-ups at the newer ski areas across Canada now show the winter photo instead of a blurry summer one.
iPhone: pop-up cards no longer hide their ✕ under the clock.
Ski heatmap now covers the backcountry across Canada (about 650 touring areas), leaves out the resorts, and counts November and May tours in the alpine.
3D map: each trail name now shows once, near the middle of the screen.
The 3D map now shows every trail name, like the flat map.
Plan a route on the 3D map: moving the start and taking a trail out now update the route on the map.
3D map on phones uses much less memory: the flat map underneath rests while 3D is on, so 3D stays open longer and moves more smoothly.
Trail and route names now show along the lines on the 3D map too.
Loops now start and finish at the parking lot closest to their trails, and never use bike park trails (those are lift access only).
Skiing 3D on phones is lighter and smoother, so it stops jumping back to the flat map at Whistler and Blackcomb.
Skiing 3D on phones: the Winter photos get sharper close up, with real bumps, gullies and trees, once you stop moving the map.
Skiing, FATMAP style: colour keys on the map, picture tiles in Layers, a short tour card with ✈ Flyover, new Flats, Elevation bands and snow layers.
Skiing 3D uses much less phone memory, so it no longer drops back to the flat map around Whistler.
Skiing 3D: last winter's real snow photos now cover ski hills, ski tours and backcountry areas across Canada, not just BC and Alberta
Skiing: every heli-skiing and cat skiing operation in Canada on the map, with terrain, season, trips, group size, price and booking. BC terrain areas shaded
Typing on a phone: the box you type in now moves up above the keyboard everywhere in the app (search boxes, notes, forms, sign-in), so you always see what you type

Adventure moto routes now use every province's 511 (closures, washouts, bridges out, roadwork, snow and ice), checked in the background every 10 minutes, and count city traffic for the hour you'll be there. Pick when you leave under the route

Search a place: type a region, range, mountain or town (like Chic-Chocs or Rogers Pass) in Skiing, Hunting, Fishing and Adventure moto and the map goes there. In Plan a route you can type where you start and where you want to go
3D map: a photo that fails to download is asked for again, so the ground no longer stays blank in big squares
Forest roads are now thin lines that look like roads, not thick bands, in every sport and in 3D
Adventure moto: Plan a route no longer makes huge detours for gates and posts beside the highway. Hurley warns when snowed in
Clouds show on the flat map only: the 3D map no longer has the cloud mist and slider
Adventure moto: tap a campsite, gas, hot spring or shop dot (also in 3D) to see what it is, how far it is, fee, water, toilets, hours, website and height.

Adventure: ADV routes now has its own button at the top (it replaces Ride, which is the Ride tab). 3D says "Loading the mountains…" until the ground shows. Hunting: legal light times stay right when the weather can't load
Adventure moto is called Adventure in the sport picker under More too, the same as the map button
Fishing: ecological reserves (no fishing allowed) show in red on the map in BC and Quebec; wildlife reserves and parks, where you can fish with an access fee, keep their own colours
Fishing: Rules starts with the main rules in short (closures open or closed today, hooks and bait, daily limits) for BC, Quebec and Ontario
Fishing: the Fishing zones and regions layer starts off (turn it on in Layers or with the Rules view)
Fishing: Boating shows motor and speed limits from hidden-spot notes and the lake's fishing rules too (like 10 hp max on Callaghan Lake), with where each comes from
Fishing: each lake's own seasons and limits on the spot card (BC, Quebec and Ontario), with open or closed today
Fishing: every layer has its own colour and picture (hook for fishing spots, boat for launches, mountain for hidden spots, tree for parks), in Layers and on the map
Fishing: fish lists for Alberta rivers and the Atlantic provinces (Nova Scotia lake surveys, fish recorded nearby, the big salmon rivers)
Fixed: leaving the iPhone app on the 3D map now brings you back to 3D, not the flat map

Adventure moto: ADV routes come in region folders, and each route shows its photo, highlights, hardest part, water crossings, ferries, permits, best months, gas and camping on the way, and trip reports.
Fishing: ocean spots show what you can keep there today (salmon, crab, prawns, bottom fish) with limits, sizes, closures and shellfish safety; BC every night from DFO, plus the Atlantic coasts
Fishing: fixes from a full test (right boating limits, honest bite score, lake depths, one Safe to eat list, no doubled launches)
Moto is now called Adventure moto.
3D map: no more grey “Map data not yet available” squares when you zoom in where the photos stop sooner (Garibaldi Lake): the nearest real photo is shown instead
Moving the map yourself (2D or 3D) stops it following you, so it no longer jumps back to your location; tap Me to follow again.
Moto: Plan a route shows your numbered points on the 2D and 3D maps, lists them to reorder, and goes around closed forest roads, locked gates, washouts, motor vehicle closures and fire closures.
Fishing: no more blue rings around the dots on the 3D map
Moto: Your bike now lists every model of 39 makes by year, with real model names and their weight, tank and fuel use.
Fishing: Route now sticks to the trails from the trailhead parking and only walks through the forest for the last bit where no trail goes
Fishing: cleaner, more modern colours for the map dots
Moto: pick your bike by year, make and model, ADV routes, ride log, check-in alarm, cell signal, snow on passes, 3D fly-through
Fishing: Green Lake boat launch in the right place, more launches, and zones and parks now show on the 3D map
New 🏍 Moto mode: dirt roads graded for your bike, mud, fuel range and route planner

All of Canada: trail closures for every BC park, 26 national parks and Ontario Parks, e-bike rules outside BC and Alberta, Quebec logging areas, ski resort runs, groomed nordic and snowmobile trails everywhere, and snow stations outside BC
Fishing: a Rules map like Hunting (regions, zones, national parks, Quebec zecs and reserves), a Buy a licence link for your province, boating limits on every restricted lake, and more boat launches

Hunting now works across Canada: Quebec zones, ZECs, wildlife reserves and outfitters, Ontario WMUs, plus zones in Manitoba, Saskatchewan, the Maritimes, Newfoundland and the Yukon, with seasons for Quebec, Ontario and Manitoba
Hunting: My hunts replaces My rides, with each hunt you tracked, its weather, what you saw, and What works
All of Canada: riding areas from Vancouver Island to Halifax and Whitehorse, 🔔 new-trail and prime loam alerts Around you anywhere, and trailheads, parking and forest roads outside BC and Alberta
Fishing: Rivers, Lakes or Ocean now colours every river, lake or the sea on the map (tap the map to clear it), and boat launches have their own layer
Fishing: a new Hidden spots layer with stocked lakes no road reaches and hike-in waters most anglers never get to, with how to get there and what bites
Fishing: tap Route on a spot for the best way to walk there, on trails and roads first, then across the easiest ground (slope, forest, wetland, creeks)
Fishing: tap a spot, pick how you fish (fly, lures, bait, trolling or ice) and see what to use for each fish there, matched to what they eat in that water this season
Fishing is easier to read: each part of a spot is one short line you tap to open, and a new layer shows public fishing spots, piers and boat launches all over Canada
The app reopens on the map you left it on: 3D or flat, and the same photos, in each sport
Faster map: it now fills in while you pan instead of after you stop, satellite photos come in quicker, and 3D opens faster and tilts up to the mountains and sky

New sport: 🎣 Fishing, all over Canada. Rules for the spot, stocked lakes, river flow vs normal, tides, hatches, safe to eat (ON, QC), a private catch log, fish ID from a photo and fresh stocking alerts
Smoother 3D map in Skiing on phones: the pins (slackcountry, gates, webcams) no longer slow every move, which could crash the 3D map
Photo find no longer takes Google's picture tags (like “Hybrid bicycle”) for trail names, so fewer wrong Best matches
Loam index now reads each soil's own wetness, so sandy trails (around Quebec City and elsewhere) no longer show 0 every day. A moon at night in the weather
Slackcountry at Revelstoke, Whitewater, RED, Fernie, Cypress, Seymour, Sun Peaks, Lake Louise and Shames: gates, lines and ways back in Skiing
Skiing: Ski access is now Approach trails, and trailhead parking shows as blue P pins. Village and resort lots are gone
Skiing: live lift status on the map, green open, orange standby, red closed. Tap a lift for its wait time and details
Slackcountry at Whistler Blackcomb: gates, lines and ways back in Skiing
Quebec and the rest of Canada: Where to ride today and Loops work there, with Quebec riding areas on the map, and the Chic-Chocs show their own avalanche forecast
Drawing a square is easy on the phone: drag its big corners, then tap Find trails here
Loops in Where to ride today: pick the distance and time, get a different loop, or leave a trail out
Photo find in the woods, and teach it with your ride photos
Same four map buttons in every sport, with names: Sport, Layers, 3D and Me
Phones: swipe up the map's search bar for the Find page, and each tool now has one place (Offline maps in Ride, My rides and Add a trail in Saved)
Layers opens as a full panel on phones, with 4 map styles: Map, Topo, Satellite, Satellite + names
Trail details open as a half sheet over the map, with loam, length, down and up at the top
A short What's new list when the app opens (you're reading it)
Sport button on the map: MTB, Skiing or Hunting in one tap
Avalanche check: route lights, terrain class, avalanche weather and alerts
Backcountry ski areas across Canada
Add a trail you know that isn't on the map
Opens faster on weak signal, and the map moves more smoothly
Live webcams in Skiing
Hunting compass and rangefinder
Rogers Pass: permit areas, today's status and huts
Skiing 3D: webcam and Rogers Pass pins stay in place
Hunting: smoother zooming
Hunting: forest types in 5 simple hunter classes
Skiing layers grouped in the Layers menu
Skiing opens on the 3D map
Skiing: tap hut dots, and a Map key
Ski heatmap: smooth lines when zoomed in
Clouds like Windy: satellite now and forecast
Which trail is this? More careful photo matches, and you can correct it
Import your Strava rides, and share rides if you want
Wildfire smoke layer
E-bike rules, closures, water and toilets, ready-made loops and spoken directions
